main_text.head: Crocodilus vnus fugientem perfequens, & alter hominem perfequentem fugiens. XXXII.
main_text.p: [woodcut illustration: a crocodile pursuing a fleeing man, and a second man pursuing a fleeing crocodile; not transcribed as text]
NIliacus qualis ferpens fugientibus inftat, Inftátes fugiens quamlibet ante ferox. Sic Vetus ille Draco, fauus mortalibus hoftis, Te reprimente fugit, te fugiente premit.

page.notes: The initial N is a large woodcut letter joined to "Iliacus". The woodcut is an emblem picture and is described only in brackets above. The epigram is set in italic with a large roman initial; the first line's word "Iliacus" follows the initial. Some letters in the epigram ("Inftátes", "Vetus") are as printed in the scan and may be uncertain.
